title: Checks for usage of flat_map(|x| x).
summary: Readability, this can be written more concisely by using flatten. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of Iterator::flat_map() where filter_map() could be used instead.
summary: filter_map() is known to always produce 0 or 1 output items per input item, rather than however many the inner iterator type produces. Therefore, it maintains the upper bound in Iterator::size_hint(), and communicates to the reader that the input items are not being expanded into multiple output items without their having to notice that the mapping function returns an Option. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for float arithmetic.
summary: For some embedded systems or kernel development, it can be useful to rule out floating-point numbers. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for (in-)equality comparisons on floating-point values (apart from zero), except in functions called *eq* (which probably implement equality for a type involving floats).
summary: Floating point calculations are usually imprecise, so asking if two values are exactly equal is asking for trouble because arriving at the same logical result via different routes (e.g. calculation versus constant) may yield different values. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for (in-)equality comparisons on constant floating-point values (apart from zero), except in functions called *eq* (which probably implement equality for a type involving floats).
summary: Floating point calculations are usually imprecise, so asking if two values are exactly equal is asking for trouble because arriving at the same logical result via different routes (e.g. calculation versus constant) may yield different values. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for statements of the form (a - b) < f32::EPSILON or (a - b) < f64::EPSILON.
summary: Note the missing .abs(). The code without .abs() is more likely to have a bug. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.
